project.name: soa_builder
project.description: Core Python package for the SoA Workbench: a FastAPI web application (domain routers, Jinja2/HTMX templates, static assets), an MCP server, and a CLI entry point for normalizing, expanding, and validating clinical trial Schedule of Activities data against USDM.

nodes.name: audit.py
nodes.summary: Central audit-trail module providing before/after change-logging helper functions for every mutable entity type in the SoA workbench (visits, activities, elements, timings, schedule timelines, instances, amendments, organizations, roles, persons, and more), each writing a row to the entity's audit table using the supplied database cursor.
nodes.languageNotes: Highly repetitive by design: each of the 30+ functions follows the identical (soa_id, action, entity_id, before, after) signature so callers can log mutations uniformly across the whole domain model.

nodes.summary: Restores the live study's entities to match a prior freeze's captured snapshot, deleting/recreating rows as needed and recording a rollback audit entry.

nodes.summary: Computes a preview of what a rollback to a given freeze would change, without applying it, by diffing the freeze snapshot against live data.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package entry point for soa_builder that re-exports the core legacy pipeline functions (normalize_soa, expand_schedule_rules, validate_imaging_schedule) as the public API via __all__.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Click-based command-line interface exposing normalize, expand, and validate subcommands that drive the legacy SoA CSV normalization, schedule-rule expansion, and imaging validation pipeline.

nodes.name: normalization.py
nodes.summary: Parses a wide-format SoA CSV into normalized dataclasses (Visit, Activity, VisitActivity, ActivityCategory, ScheduleRule) and writes them to per-entity CSVs and a SQLite database for downstream schedule expansion.

nodes.name: schedule.py
nodes.summary: Expands normalized schedule rules (cyclical, weekly, daily patterns) into concrete projected activity occurrences across a study horizon, given a start date and cycle configuration.

nodes.name: validation.py
nodes.summary: Extracts imaging-related visit/activity events from normalized rows and validates that consecutive imaging events fall within an expected interval tolerance, used by the CLI validate command.

nodes.name: _load_rules
nodes.summary: Loads schedule_rules.csv from a normalized directory and converts each row into a RuleStub for schedule expansion.

nodes.name: _load_visits
nodes.summary: Loads visits.csv from a normalized directory and converts each row into a VisitStub keyed for schedule expansion.

nodes.name: cmd_normalize
nodes.summary: Click command implementing 'soa-builder normalize': reads a wide SoA CSV and writes normalized CSV/SQLite artifacts via normalize_soa.

nodes.name: cmd_expand
nodes.summary: Click command implementing 'soa-builder expand': loads normalized rules/visits, expands them into scheduled instances via expand_schedule_rules, and writes JSON/CSV output.

nodes.name: cmd_validate
nodes.summary: Click command implementing 'soa-builder validate': loads normalized CSVs, extracts imaging events, and validates their interval spacing via validate_imaging_schedule.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Module entry point invoking the Click cli() group when the script is run directly.

nodes.name: parse_window
nodes.summary: Parses a visit window (day ranges, +/- day offsets) out of a raw visit header string using several regex patterns.

nodes.name: extract_visit_code
nodes.summary: Extracts a canonical visit code (e.g. V1, C1D1) from a raw visit header using regex.

nodes.name: build_visits
nodes.summary: Builds the ordered list of Visit dataclasses from wide-format CSV header columns, deriving window, code, and category for each.

nodes.name: build_visit_activities
nodes.summary: Builds VisitActivity junction records linking activities to visits based on cell values in the wide CSV, capturing required/conditional flags and repeat patterns.

nodes.name: build_schedule_rules
nodes.summary: Derives ScheduleRule records for repeating/conditional activity cells, capturing the raw pattern text later consumed by schedule expansion.

nodes.name: normalize_soa
nodes.summary: Top-level orchestrator that reads a wide SoA CSV, builds all normalized entities (visits, activities, visit-activities, categories, rules), writes them to per-entity CSV files, and persists them into a SQLite database.

nodes.name: Visit
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a normalized study visit with sequence, window, code, repeat pattern, and category.

nodes.name: Activity
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a normalized study activity with an id and name.

nodes.name: VisitActivity
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing the junction between a visit and an activity, including status and required/conditional flags.

nodes.name: ActivityCategory
nodes.summary: Dataclass mapping an activity to a classified category.

nodes.name: ScheduleRule
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a raw repeating/conditional scheduling rule extracted from the wide CSV, later consumed by schedule expansion.

nodes.name: parse_pattern_interval_days
nodes.summary: Parses a schedule rule's pattern text (e.g. Q3W, QW, every N weeks, QD) into an interval-in-days value using multiple regex patterns.

nodes.name: derive_nominal_day_for_visit
nodes.summary: Derives the nominal study day for a given visit stub by inspecting its name/label for cycle-day or week/day markers.

nodes.name: get_horizon_days
nodes.summary: Computes the total number of days to project schedule instances across, based on cycle count/length and follow-up weeks.

nodes.name: expand_schedule_rules
nodes.summary: Core schedule expansion engine: projects each ScheduleRule into concrete dated Instance occurrences across cycles and follow-up, honoring interval patterns, cycle lengths, max occurrences, and pattern filters.

nodes.name: VisitStub
nodes.summary: Lightweight visit representation used by the schedule module, decoupled from the full normalization Visit dataclass to avoid circular imports.

nodes.name: RuleStub
nodes.summary: Lightweight schedule rule representation consumed by expand_schedule_rules, mirroring ScheduleRule's fields.

nodes.name: Instance
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single projected scheduled activity occurrence with nominal day, projected date, and anchor visit/activity.

nodes.name: derive_nominal_day
nodes.summary: Derives a nominal study day from a visit label by matching week/day/cycle-day patterns.

nodes.name: extract_imaging_events
nodes.summary: Filters visit-activity rows down to imaging-related activities and produces a sorted list of ImagingEvent records with derived nominal days.

nodes.name: validate_imaging_schedule
nodes.summary: Checks that consecutive imaging events fall within an expected interval (in weeks) plus/minus a day tolerance, returning a list of violation messages.

nodes.name: ImagingEvent
nodes.summary: Dataclass pairing a visit name with its derived nominal day, used for imaging interval validation.

nodes.name: server.py
nodes.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing 11 tools over stdio for interacting with the SoA workbench: listing/creating SoAs, visits, and activities, assigning activities to scheduled instances, retrieving the visits-by-activities matrix, and generating USDM/Define-JSON documents. Registered as the `soa-mcp` console script and picked up by Claude Code via `.mcp.json`.
nodes.languageNotes: Tool handlers are dispatched through a name-to-function lookup table (_dispatch); DB access reuses soa_builder.web.db._connect and heavier USDM/Define-JSON generation is lazily imported inside handlers to avoid unnecessary import-time cost.

nodes.name: _dispatch
nodes.summary: Routes an incoming MCP tool call by name to its corresponding private handler function, raising ValueError for unknown tool names.

nodes.name: _create_soa
nodes.summary: Handler for the create_soa MCP tool; validates the required name argument, inserts a new Schedule of Activities row, and commits or rolls back the transaction on error.

nodes.name: _get_soa
nodes.summary: Handler for the get_soa MCP tool; fetches metadata for a single Schedule of Activities by id, raising ValueError if not found.

nodes.name: _list_visits
nodes.summary: Handler for the list_visits MCP tool; returns the visit definitions belonging to a given Schedule of Activities.

nodes.name: _create_visit
nodes.summary: Handler for the create_visit MCP tool; validates visit name/label/type, computes the next monotonic visit UID, and inserts the new visit row within a transaction.

nodes.name: _list_activities
nodes.summary: Handler for the list_activities MCP tool; returns study activities defined for a given Schedule of Activities.

nodes.name: _create_activity
nodes.summary: Handler for the create_activity MCP tool; validates activity name/label/description, computes the next monotonic activity UID, and inserts the new activity row within a transaction.

nodes.name: _assign_instance_activity
nodes.summary: Handler for the assign_instance_activity MCP tool; marks an activity as scheduled at a given Scheduled Activity Instance, updating status and committing the change.

nodes.name: _get_soa_matrix
nodes.summary: Handler for the get_soa_matrix MCP tool; builds and returns the visits-by-activities matrix for a Schedule of Activities by joining visit, activity, and assignment data.

nodes.name: _get_usdm_json
nodes.summary: Handler for the get_usdm_json MCP tool; validates the requested USDM component name against the allowed list and delegates generation to the web usdm_json router's _build helper.

nodes.name: _get_define_json

layers.name: API Layer
layers.description: FastAPI router modules under web/routers/ implementing the domain-specific REST and HTMX UI endpoints (visits, activities, arms, epochs, elements, amendments, estimands, terminology browsers, freezes, USDM/DAIR export, and more).

layers.name: Presentation Layer
layers.description: Jinja2/HTMX HTML templates and static assets (CSS, JS, help pages) that render the SoA Workbench UI and are swapped into the page by router responses.

layers.name: Types Layer
layers.description: Pydantic request/response models in web/schemas.py, imported across nearly all routers to validate and shape API payloads.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Shared business-logic helpers and the cross-cutting audit trail (web/utils.py, web/audit.py) that routers call into for common operations and before/after change logging.

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: SQLite persistence: the canonical connection helper (db.py), schema initialization, and migration runner that every router and generator depends on for storage.

layers.name: Configuration Layer
layers.description: Application bootstrap and settings: the FastAPI app factory/lifespan wiring (app.py) and CDISC CT codelist configuration (codelist_config.py) that drive UI dropdown behavior.

layers.name: CLI / Legacy Pipeline Layer
layers.description: The original normalize/expand/validate command-line pipeline (cli.py, normalization.py, schedule.py, validation.py) and the package root, still used by the web layer's USDM generation flows.

layers.name: Integration Layer
layers.description: The Model Context Protocol server (mcp/server.py) that exposes SoA Workbench data and operations as tools for external MCP clients.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: web/app.py is the heart of the FastAPI web application: it creates the app instance, runs the lifespan startup (database initialization plus sequential schema migrations), registers every domain router, and hosts the SoA matrix build/render logic along with bulk export endpoints (XLSX/HTML/PDF/CSV). With the highest fan-out in the codebase (over 100 outgoing edges), this file is the natural starting point -- everything the workbench does is wired together here.

tour.title: Package Public API
tour.description: Before diving into the web layer, it helps to see what soa_builder exposes as its public surface. __init__.py re-exports the three core legacy pipeline functions -- normalize_soa, expand_schedule_rules, and validate_imaging_schedule -- as the package's __all__. This tells you the project actually ships two parallel systems: the modern FastAPI/SQLite web app (Step 1) and an older CSV-based CLI pipeline, which you'll revisit later in the tour.

tour.title: Database Connection & Schema Bootstrap
tour.description: web/db.py provides the single canonical `_connect()` helper used across the entire web app: it resolves the correct SQLite file (auto-switching to a test database under pytest), and opens connections in WAL mode with a busy timeout to tolerate concurrent HTMX requests. web/initialize_database.py complements it with `_init_db`, the large function that creates every core table -- studies, arms, epochs, visits, activities, cells, timelines, instances, and audit tables -- on a brand-new database. Together these two files are the persistence foundation that app.py's lifespan (Step 1) calls at startup.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite's WAL (Write-Ahead Log) mode allows concurrent readers alongside a single writer, which is important for a multi-request HTMX UI hitting the same file-based database.

tour.title: Schema Migrations
tour.description: Real databases evolve, and web/migrate_database.py is where that evolution is tracked: roughly 108 small, idempotent migration functions (new columns, new tables, audit tables, backfills, data repairs) are each imported and invoked in sequence by app.py's lifespan startup. This file has the second-highest fan-out in the codebase, reflecting how every schema change the project has ever needed lives here as a discrete, replayable function rather than a single monolithic schema file.
tour.languageLesson: Idempotent migrations can be safely re-run without side effects (e.g. checking column existence with PRAGMA table_info before ALTER TABLE), which is what lets the whole list run unconditionally on every startup.

tour.title: Audit Trail
tour.description: Building on the persistence layer from Steps 3-4, web/audit.py provides before/after change-logging helpers for every mutable entity in the workbench -- visits, activities, elements, timings, schedule timelines, instances, amendments, organizations, roles, and more. Each helper writes a row to the entity's audit table using a shared database cursor, meaning any router that mutates data (Step 7) can log full change history with one function call. With 26 incoming references, this module is depended upon almost everywhere mutations happen.

tour.title: Pydantic Schemas & Shared Utilities
tour.description: web/schemas.py is the central Pydantic validation module: it defines Create/Update payload models for every mutable USDM entity (activities, elements, visits, timings, arms, epochs, amendments, and more), including validators for ISO 8601 durations and timing-window consistency. web/utils.py is the workbench's service layer -- it integrates with the CDISC Library API (with caching), generates monotonic UIDs for dozens of entity types, and offers USDM/database lookup helpers. Both files are among the most fanned-in modules in the project, since nearly every router (Step 7) imports request schemas from one and helper functions from the other.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic models double as both request validation and self-documenting API contracts -- FastAPI uses the same classes to generate OpenAPI schema documentation automatically.

tour.title: The Router / API Layer
tour.description: Domain logic lives in web/routers/, one module per USDM entity family. web/routers/activities.py handles Activity CRUD plus CDISC Biomedical Concept association; web/routers/elements.py, cells.py, visits.py, and schedule_timelines.py implement the structural (StudyElement, StudyCell) and temporal (Visit, ScheduleTimeline, ScheduledActivityInstance) sides of the SoA model described in this project's domain knowledge. Every router follows the same pattern seen in app.py: a REST endpoint plus a parallel HTMX UI endpoint that returns an HTML partial for in-page swaps, using the schemas (Step 6) for validation and audit.py (Step 5) for change logging.

tour.title: Amendments & USDM Export
tour.description: Two routers show how the workbench connects clinical trial change management to the formal USDM standard. web/routers/amendments.py implements CRUD for protocol amendments and their many sub-entities (impacts, geographic scopes, subject enrollments, governance dates). web/routers/usdm_json.py serves the generated USDM JSON and Define-JSON views, delegating the actual generation work to the separate `usdm` package's generators -- this is where the workbench's internal SQLite model gets transformed into standards-compliant USDM artifacts.

tour.title: Configuration: Controlled Terminology Codelists
tour.description: web/codelist_config.py defines the CDISC controlled-terminology codelist codes (epoch type, arm type, role type, objective/endpoint level, intervention role/type/unit, and more) that back every dropdown in the UI. Each is overridable via a CODELIST_* environment variable read once at import time, letting a deployment point a dropdown at an alternate codelist without touching code. With 13 incoming references, this module is the single source of truth that both the routers (Step 7) and templates (Step 10) rely on for consistent terminology.

tour.title: The Presentation Layer
tour.description: The UI is server-rendered Jinja2 plus HTMX rather than a separate frontend framework. web/templates/base.html is the site-wide layout -- HTML shell, collapsible sidebar navigation, and the {% block content %} extension point every other template inherits from; with 42 incoming references it is by far the most depended-upon file in the entire project. web/static/style.css supplies the shared `am-`/`fz-` utility-class design system used across all templates, and web/static/bc_explorer.js drives the one significant piece of client-side interactivity: filtering and rendering the CDISC Biomedical Concept explorer.
tour.languageLesson: HTMX lets server-rendered HTML partials replace fragments of the page on user interaction (via hx-get/hx-post attributes), avoiding the need for a client-side JavaScript framework while still getting SPA-like responsiveness.

tour.title: The Legacy CLI Pipeline
tour.description: Alongside the modern web app, soa_builder still ships its original command-line pipeline, exposed as three subcommands. cli.py is the Click-based entry point (normalize, expand, validate); normalization.py parses a wide-format SoA CSV into normalized dataclasses (Visit, Activity, VisitActivity, ScheduleRule) and writes them to per-entity CSVs and SQLite; schedule.py expands those normalized rules -- cyclical, weekly, daily patterns -- into concrete projected activity occurrences across a study horizon; and validation.py checks that imaging events fall within expected interval tolerances. This is the pre-USDM, file-based workflow that predates the FastAPI app from Step 1, and __init__.py (Step 2) re-exports exactly these three functions.

tour.title: MCP Integration Layer
tour.description: mcp/server.py exposes the SoA workbench over the Model Context Protocol, offering 11 tools over stdio for listing/creating SoAs, visits, and activities, assigning activities to scheduled instances, and retrieving USDM/Define-JSON output. This is what lets an AI agent (such as Claude Code, via the soa-workbench MCP tools referenced elsewhere in this project) interact with the same underlying data model that the FastAPI routers (Step 7) and CLI (Step 11) expose to humans -- a third, programmatic front door onto the same persistence layer from Steps 3-5.
